description: VELTRIXA is a team of university students passionate about technology, innovation, and problem-solving. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we are working on “Flame in Freefall,” exploring how technology and AI can help make microgravity combustion research more accessible and understandable.🚀🔥
summary:
Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data

What we developed:
VELTRIXA is a space data platform that helps people make decisions. VELTRIXA looks at NASA Physical Sciences Informatics studies about how fires behave in space settings like lunar bases, Mars habitats and pressurized rovers.
How does VELTRIXA address the challenge? 
VELTRIXA pulls NASA PSI data, such as ACME, BASS, FLEX and SAFFIRE experiments and combines it with a rule‑based scoring system and a chat interface. VELTRIXA lets users filter fire studies by the type of habitat, by the goal they want such as habitat safety, predictive modelling or next‑generation fire suppression and by oxygen levels for example a pure‑oxygen cabin or an Artemis Moon base atmosphere.
Why is VELTRIXA important? 
Fire safety is a life‑support challenge for long space missions. VELTRIXA turns microgravity fire data into clear useful information for mission planners and scientists.

Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data

What we developed:

Project Details:

• VELTRIXA offers an exploration dashboard and a backend API powered by Pandas. The API includes endpoints like /api/rank and /api/chat, which rank NASA combustion experiments based on relevance. The system supports filtering, side-by-side comparisons of experiments, a searchable data grid and a context-aware assistant. This assistant can answer questions related to microgravity fire safety.

• Built using HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript and powered by a Python Flask / Pandas, backend VELTRIXA looks at factors. These factors include habitat relevance which is rated from 1 to 5. It also checks goal alignment and oxygen-enrichment multipliers. VELTRIXA works completely offline because it has datasets built in. These datasets are in a file called data.js. At the time VELTRIXA can also do analysis and as we move on, we will start operating VELTRIXA at the server side as well.

Benefits:

• Mission Safety looks at which experiments are the same size as spacecraft for example SAFFIRE give the best examples of how fire behaves inside a cabin and this can help us understand risks.

• Cross-Disciplinary Access helps to bridge the gap between raw NASA PSI reports and the planning that is done for missions.

• Terrestrial Spinoffs highlight how research from space improves fire detection, on Earth the detection of aerosols and the safety of firefighters.

• We hope to achieve to help space mission planners, teachers and people who judge hackathons with the initiative of a tool that we created that uses real data. This tool shows why studying how fires burn in space is important and it helps keep explorers safe when they go to the Moon, Mars and even farther places.

• Languages: Python, HTML5, CSS3,JavaScript.

• Frameworks & Libraries: Python Flask, Pandas.

• Development & Design Tools: Git, VS Code, WebP image processing, Custom SVG iconography.

Use of SI:

• Tools Used: Large Language Models (LLMs) and code generation assistants were used during development of the website to speed up front end layout prototyping and improve documentation structure.

• Compliance Statement: All content and code generated comply with NASA Space Apps guidelines and do not use, change or misuse NASA logos, flags or official mission identifiers.
